title: ModelUsage
description: The `data` payload of `dmtool -m <model> model usage` (CLI-SPEC §6) — the model-wide usage/audit read. `usage` maps EVERY field path to the full names of the rules and computations that READ it (an empty array = read by nothing); `documentUniquenessCriteria` maps the fields a uniqueness criterion names to those criteria; `unreferenced` is the subset of fields nothing reads and no criterion names. Reading includes reaching the field through an ancestor GROUP operand, because the kernel expands a group operand recursively to every field below it: `AllFieldsFilled(/Order/Address)` reads `/Order/Address/Region/Code` while naming neither. This is DELIBERATELY wider than `where-used`, which answers the exact question 'which rules name this entity?' and does not list a rule that names an enclosing group — so the two differ on exactly those fields, by design. It is also deliberately CONSERVATIVE: it answers 'a rule reaches into this group', not 'this particular field enters that operator's expansion'. A group-list predicate over a repeatable group counts instantiated ROWS rather than reading each field's value, so a field under such a group is reported read though that operator never inspects it. Erring toward 'read' is the correct direction for an audit whose `unreferenced` half is acted on as safe-to-delete. Fields are in model order; referrers are sorted.

usage.description: field path → the rule/computation full names that read it, whether by naming it or by naming an ancestor group (empty array = nothing reads the field)

items.description: a referencing rule's or computation's full name

documentUniquenessCriteria.description: field path → the names of the document uniqueness criteria that name it, for every field a criterion names, a mounted field included; a criterion is addressed by its name, since A12 gives it no path

unreferenced.description: the fields no rule or computation reads and no document uniqueness criterion names — the audit headline (candidates for removal, or a missing rule)
